# Test-only PDF signature fixtures

These documents are generated and owned by this project. They are security-policy fixtures, not examples of a trusted or legally effective signature.

Generate with `bun tests/helpers/generate-pdf-signatures.ts`. The generator creates RSA private keys in an OS temporary directory, creates the PDFs and public certificates, then removes the entire temporary workspace in `finally`. No private keys are retained. Regeneration deliberately produces new keys/CMS values; `checksums.json` records the generated artifacts and OpenSSL version.

| File                                     | What is actually verified                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `signed-valid.pdf`                       | Detached SHA-256 CMS signature made with the self-signed `valid-signer.pem`; `/ByteRange` covers the complete PDF except the reserved `/Contents` token. Cryptographic integrity verifies independently with OpenSSL. Certificate validity is 2020-01-01 through 2040-01-01. |
| `signed-invalid.pdf`                     | Same CMS and byte ranges as `signed-valid.pdf`, with one covered page-content byte changed. CMS integrity verification must fail. The PDF structure remains parseable.                                                                                                       |
| `signed-expired.pdf`                     | Independently signed PDF whose detached CMS integrity verifies, but the self-signed certificate expired on 2021-01-01. This separates signature integrity from certificate-date validation. No trusted timestamp is present.                                                 |
| `certification-structure.pdf`            | A valid detached CMS plus catalog `/Perms` → `/DocMDP` and a DocMDP transform structure. The test proves CMS integrity and conservative structure detection; it does not certify reader-specific enforcement, identity, or standards conformance.                            |
| `timestamp-structure.pdf`                | **Synthetic policy marker only:** `/Type /DocTimeStamp` and `/ETSI.RFC3161` with placeholder contents. This is not an authentic timestamp token, and no timestamp-validity claim is made.                                                                                    |
| `valid-signer.pem`, `expired-signer.pem` | Public self-signed test certificates only. These are not publicly trusted CA credentials.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

`tests/integration/api-pdf-signatures.test.ts` reconstructs signed coverage from `/ByteRange`, parses the DER length rather than trimming zero bytes, verifies detached CMS using only the published signer certificate, checks that tampering fails integrity, and evaluates certificate dates at the fixed instant 2030-01-01 UTC. Explicitly trusting a local test certificate for that date check is not a claim of public trust, identity verification, revocation checking, or a trusted signing time.

Every document—including the synthetic timestamp structure—is required to remain byte-identical when Squeezit skips it in default and max mode. A preexisting API output destination must also remain unchanged.
